using System;
using System.Net.Http;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.AzureOpenAI;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Http;
using Xunit;
using Moq;

namespace Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Tests
{
    public class AzureOpenAIServiceCollectionExtensionsTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void AddAzureOpenAIChatClient_RegistersIChatClientFactory_AndCallsGetServiceOnServiceProvider()
        {
            // Arrange
            var services = new ServiceCollection();

            var mockLoggerFactory = new Mock<ILoggerFactory>();

            var mockServiceProvider = new Mock<IServiceProvider>();
            mockServiceProvider.Setup(sp => sp.GetService(typeof(ILoggerFactory))).Returns(mockLoggerFactory.Object);

            // We add a HttpClient to the services to satisfy HttpClientProvider.GetHttpClient call
            services.AddHttpClient();

            // Act
            services.AddAzureOpenAIChatClient(
                deploymentName: "testDeployment",
                endpoint: "https://test.endpoint",
                apiKey: "testApiKey");

            // Build the service provider from the collection
            var serviceProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider();

            // We resolve the IChatClient using the factory registered in AddKeyedSingleton
            // The factory internally calls serviceProvider.GetService<ILoggerFactory>()
            // We simulate this by creating a scope with a service provider that returns our mockLoggerFactory
            var chatClient = serviceProvider.GetService<IChatClient>();

            // Assert
            // We cannot directly assert the internal call to GetService on IServiceProvider in the extension method,
            // but we can assert that the serviceProvider resolves IChatClient without error.
            Assert.NotNull(chatClient);
        }
    }
}

using System;

{
    public class AzureOpenAIServiceCollectionExtensionsTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void AddAzureOpenAIChatClient_RegistersIChatClientFactory_AndResolvesIChatClient()
        {
            // Arrange
            var services = new ServiceCollection();

            // Add a mock ILoggerFactory to the service collection to be resolved by the factory
            var mockLoggerFactory = new Mock<ILoggerFactory>();
            services.AddSingleton(mockLoggerFactory.Object);

            // Add a HttpClient to the service collection to satisfy HttpClientProvider.GetHttpClient call
            services.AddHttpClient();

            // Act
            services.AddAzureOpenAIChatClient(
                deploymentName: "testDeployment",
                endpoint: "https://test.endpoint",
                apiKey: "testApiKey");

            var serviceProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider();

            // Resolve the IChatClient from the service provider
            var chatClient = serviceProvider.GetService<IChatClient>();

            // Assert
            Assert.NotNull(chatClient);
        }
    }
}

The `AddHttpClient` method is part of the `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` package, which might not be referenced in the test project, so I will remove that call since the tested code uses a fallback for HttpClient if none is provided.
